title: The IAM chain: one command, two atlases
lead: One sample goes in, and one command reads it. The chain takes arrays and sequencing alike, and reads each against the healthy atlas measured with its own chemistry: IAM-Atlas v2.1 for arrays, the IAM Sequencing Atlas for sequenced samples. Healthy comes only from the atlases, never from other samples in the same run, laboratory or study.

The IAM-Deconvolver reads first: which cells are in the sample, and in what shares. Then each cell it finds is read against its own healthy profile in the atlas. IAM-A needs no outside reference at all: it reads a person's cells against themselves.

Commissioned, each on a test written and sealed before its data was seen: IAM-Atlas v2.1 for its first uses, where on the jobs an atlas is used for it beat both published reference atlases; the IAM-Deconvolver for blood-cell shares; and IAM-A. Met-A, the C-Score and Group-A were first commissioned against references taken from other samples, and are being re-commissioned against the atlas alone.
These are research instruments, not a diagnostic test. Where the lines on the gauge belong for cancer is for cancer researchers to find; these are the instruments to find it with.
